AUTHOR: Sorrenti, A; Russo, LG; Samarasinghe, S; Palazzo, S; Spampinato, C
TITLE: Weakly Supervised MaxN Estimation in Baited Remote Underwater Videos
VENUE: 2025 IEEE/CVF INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON COMPUTER VISION WORKSHOPS, ICCVW
DATA: 287 BRUV videos (VONGOLA project) with weak per-video, per-species MaxN + timestamp labels; 4,354 sampled frames plus mined negative frames
V_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'the visual quality of the footage is often affected by... moving algae or suspended particles. Additionally, video clarity varied significantly between deployments'
D_EV: Sec. 4.3: 'videos were randomly assigned to the training, validation, and test sets in proportions of 70%, 10%, and 20%... To prevent data leakage, the split was performed at the video level'
R_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'The pipeline was evaluated on a dataset consisting of 287 underwater videos collected in the lower Tyrrhenian Sea' (single dataset)
C_EV: Sec. 3.2: 'with θpca being a hyperparameter, which we empirically set to 0.65'; 'We discard any box where this fraction is below a threshold θfrac = 0.1'
E_EV: Abstract/Table 1: 'Our method achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 4.23 on fish counts ranging from 1 to about 300' (vs annotated MaxN of the same videos)
ARCH: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 features + modified ResNet-18 regression head; YOLOv12 (FastSAM/SAM2-bootstrapped) + DINOv2-PCA filtering for negative mining
METR: MSE, MAE, relative error of per-species MaxN
NOTE: Thresholds (θpca 0.65, θfrac 0.1, τ=3) apply to the coarse detector used for negative-frame mining, 'empirically set' without justification -> C1=Y, C_ALL=N; final MaxN regression has no score threshold (verifier may prefer C_ALL=NR). Ground truth is human MaxN from the same BRUV videos. Habitat type not stated (ENV=NR). Evaluation is on frames sampled around annotated MaxN events and mined negatives, not full-video MaxN.
